items.title: CVE-2026-104809 (HIGH 8.4): DigitalCanion has discovered a vulnerability that allows an attacker to cause the system to load an attacker-…
items.one_liner: A high-severity shared object loading vulnerability in Mitel Linux VMs requires immediate patching.
items.summary: DigitalCanion has discovered a high-severity vulnerability designated CVE-2026-104809 in a Mitel Linux virtual machine, carrying a CVSS base score of 8.4. The flaw allows an attacker to force the system into loading a malicious .so file instead of the legitimate module due to a predictable module name and inadequate origin verification. A privileged process executes the malicious shared object, resulting in arbitrary code execution and full system compromise. The vulnerability was officially added to CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on October 5, 2026.
items.bottom_line: Unauthenticated shared object loading in Mitel Linux virtual machines leads to full root compromise via arbitrary code execution.

items.title: Cisco NX-OS Software NX-API Remote Code Execution Vulnerability
items.one_liner: Cisco NX-OS software contains an unauthenticated RCE flaw in its NX-API feature requiring immediate updates.
items.summary: A high-severity remote code execution vulnerability exists in the NX-API feature of Cisco NX-OS Software, enabling unauthenticated remote attackers to execute arbitrary code with root privileges or trigger a denial of service. The flaw stems from insufficient input validation of HTTP requests submitted to the NX-API interface, which can cause process crashes and device reloads. Cisco has released official software updates to resolve the issue with no available workarounds.
key_facts: Impact: Remote Code Execution with root privileges / DoS
items.bottom_line: Unauthenticated HTTP requests to Cisco NX-OS NX-API can execute arbitrary root commands or cause service disruptions.

items.title: Attackers Hijack .gh, .sl, and .as Registries to Obtain Certificates for Google Domains
items.one_liner: Compromised .gh, .sl, and .as ccTLD registries allowed attackers to obtain and abuse HTTPS certificates for Google domains.
items.summary: Attackers compromised the country-code top-level domain registries for Ghana (.gh), Sierra Leone (.sl), and American Samoa (.as) by altering authoritative DNS records to obtain unauthorized HTTPS certificates. Certificate Transparency logs revealed at least 12 domain-validated certificates issued for Google and YouTube names between September 22 and 27 by Let's Encrypt and ZeroSSL. Although Google's internal systems were uncompromised, the certificates exposed encrypted traffic to potential interception. Google mitigated the incident by leveraging Chrome's CRLSets to block the certificates and coordinating rapid revocations with the issuing certificate authorities.
items.bottom_line: Attackers hijacked ccTLD DNS records to generate unauthorized HTTPS certificates for Google and other global brands, requiring emergency browser blocks and revocations.

items.title: Alert: FortiBleed remains active campaign, can lock out users or lead to ransomware attacks
items.one_liner: The FortiBleed campaign continues to compromise hundreds of thousands of Fortinet firewalls and VPNs, locking out users and serving as an entry point for ransomware.
items.summary: The FortiBleed campaign continues to target internet-exposed Fortinet firewalls and VPN gateways using compromised credentials to lock out administrators and facilitate ransomware deployments. Originally uncovered with over 86,644 compromised devices, wider investigations indicate over 400,000 to 450,000 devices have been targeted in the broader operation. Attackers leverage unauthorized access to create new admin accounts and change passwords, rendering standard patching and password resets insufficient. Government agencies including the FBI and Secret Service warn that initial access brokers are supplying access to ransomware affiliates such as INC/Lynx and Payload, and recommend restricting external management and enforcing multifactor authentication.
key_facts: Initial discovery scale: 86,644 compromised devices across 194 countries
items.bottom_line: Fortinet devices exposed to the internet face active credential compromise and administrative lockout via FortiBleed, frequently preceding ransomware deployment.

items.title: FBI disrupts Chinese hacking tools used to breach critical infrastructure
items.one_liner: FBI domain seizures disrupt Flax Typhoon and Integrity Tech infrastructure used for global critical infrastructure scanning and intrusions.
items.summary: The FBI seized seven domains operated by China-based Integrity Technology Group on behalf of the Flax Typhoon hacking group, disrupting two platforms known as MicroScan and FishHub used to compromise critical infrastructure. MicroScan combined vulnerability scanning with Mirai botnets to target organizations including a South Carolina power company, Japanese and Polish airports, and Taiwanese energy and academic institutions. FishHub facilitated spear-phishing and malware delivery, granting unauthorized remote access and enabling data exfiltration across more than 20 organizations. United States authorities worked alongside international partners and domestic agencies to issue joint advisories and display seizure notices on the offending domains.
items.bottom_line: Seven domains supporting Chinese state-sponsored cyber operations against critical infrastructure have been seized by the FBI.

items.one_liner: Palo Alto Networks GlobalProtect on Windows is vulnerable to MITM SYSTEM code execution via CVE-2026-0298 in PLAP configurations.
items.summary: An improper input validation vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-0298 with a medium severity rating, affects the Windows Pre-Logon Access Provider (PLAP) component of the Palo Alto Networks GlobalProtect app. A network-adjacent man-in-the-middle attacker can exploit the flaw to execute arbitrary code with SYSTEM privileges on targeted Windows devices, specifically impacting configurations using SAML authentication with the Connect Before Logon (CBL) feature. The vulnerability affects GlobalProtect app versions 6.3.3 and earlier, 6.2.8 and earlier, and 6.0.0 through 6.0.14 on Windows. Palo Alto Networks has confirmed there is no active malicious exploitation and provided configuration-based mitigations.

items.title: AI-powered fuzzing with the GitHub Security Lab Taskflow Agent
items.one_liner: GitHub's new autonomous fuzzing agent automates harness writing and crash triage for C/C++ repositories.
items.summary: The GitHub Security Lab has released the Fuzzing Taskflow, an autonomous fuzzing pipeline built on top of the Taskflow Agent framework designed for C and C++ projects. Developers can point the tool at any GitHub repository slug to automatically install software like AFL++, clone the repository, identify entry points, write fuzz harnesses, run campaigns, and triage crashes. The agent utilizes Claude Sonnet 5 by default to bypass frontier model guardrails and operates using shell drivers, taskflow YAMLs, and MCP tools. Because the agent executes build commands directly on the host without containerization, users are warned to run it exclusively within disposable environments.
items.bottom_line: Autonomous LLM fuzzing agents can manage the entire vulnerability discovery pipeline from harness generation to crash triage, but require isolated execution environments.

items.title: Tensorlake npm Package Compromised to Deliver Shai-Hulud Credential-Stealing Worm
items.one_liner: The npm package tensorlake was compromised to distribute the Shai-Hulud credential-stealing worm and development environment persistence.
items.summary: The npm package 'tensorlake' was compromised in a supply chain attack involving malicious version 0.5.144, which delivers the Shai-Hulud credential-stealing worm. The payload utilizes an obfuscated loader and Bun runtime to harvest sensitive tokens, SSH keys, configuration files, and cloud credentials, while dropping the HackBrowserData binary. The worm establishes persistence, injects malicious VS Code and Claude configuration tasks to execute upon opening projects, and attempts exfiltration via custom endpoints or public GitHub repositories.
items.bottom_line: Version 0.5.144 of the tensorlake npm package contains a malicious worm that harvests cloud credentials, sets up persistence, and poisons local developer workspaces.

items.one_liner: A ransomware attack on SoftBank subsidiary IDC Frontier knocks out IDCF Cloud services for hundreds of Japanese clients.
items.summary: IDC Frontier suffered a ransomware attack that disrupted its IDCF Cloud service and forced the shutdown of a data center cluster in East Japan Region 1, impacting 495 companies and local governments. Threat actors claimed to have encrypted 225 databases holding 3.6 PB of data, reached 239 hypervisors, sealed 16,000 VM disks, and wiped 554,153 snapshots within minutes. In response, IDC Frontier isolated affected systems and temporarily disabled customer access to management consoles across all regions. The incident coincides with a sharp rise in cyberattacks across Japan targeting access control and authentication weaknesses.

items.summary: US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth announced that the military execution of former US Army major Nidal Hasan by firing squad will be publicly livestreamed on December 3. items.title: CVE-2026-19184 (HIGH 8.4): The NXP GAU ADC driver (drivers/adc/adc_mcux_gau_adc.c) validated the caller-supplied sequence->buffer_size,…
items.one_liner: CVE-2026-19184 is a CVSS 8.4 out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the NXP GAU ADC Zephyr driver allowing potential local privilege escalation.
items.summary: CVE-2026-19184 is a high-severity (CVSS 8.4) memory corruption vulnerability in the NXP GAU ADC driver within Zephyr. The driver improperly validated a caller-supplied buffer size in bytes against the expected sample count, causing conversion results past the buffer's midpoint to be written out of bounds. On builds with CONFIG_USERSPACE=y on NXP RW61x SoCs, a user-mode thread with access to the ADC device object can submit an undersized buffer and trigger the supervisor-mode work-queue handler to perform arbitrary-length and arbitrary-destination memory writes. This leads to kernel memory corruption, system crashes, or privilege escalation. The issue has been patched by implementing proper buffer size validation using shared helper functions and correcting loop bounds.
key_facts: Affected Component: NXP GAU ADC driver (drivers/adc/adc_mcux_gau_adc.c) in Zephyr
Affected Hardware: NXP RW61x SoCs with GAU ADC node enabled
items.bottom_line: An input validation flaw in the NXP GAU ADC Zephyr driver (CVE-2026-19184) allows local user-space threads to achieve kernel memory corruption and potential privilege escalation.

items.title: Windows Exploitation Techniques: Dangling COM Object Registrations
items.one_liner: Dangling COM registrations in Windows allow for privilege escalation via malicious DLL injection.
items.summary: Researchers have detailed a privilege escalation technique targeting a dangling COM object registration in Windows, identified as CVE-2026-66804. The vulnerability stems from a missing server executable for the CrossDevice COM object, allowing an attacker to place a malicious DLL in a user-writable directory to achieve code execution in privileged processes. This serves as an alternative exploit path following the incomplete fix for the 'Dark Elevator' bug (CVE-2026-50343). The researchers demonstrate that custom COM marshaling can be used to force the loading of the malicious DLL into a privileged service.
items.bottom_line: Attackers can achieve privilege escalation by placing a malicious DLL in a predictable path to exploit a dangling COM object registration.

items.title: Evolution of Web3 in Cloud Supply Chain Attacks
items.one_liner: Attackers are shifting to Web3-based C2 and smart contracts to maintain persistent, dynamic control over botnets targeting CI/CD pipelines.
items.summary: Threat actors are increasingly adopting Web3 and blockchain-based smart contracts for command-and-control (C2) infrastructure to bypass static detection. Campaigns like 'ChainDrop' target developer environments and CI/CD pipelines to harvest cloud identity tokens, service account keys, and deployment secrets. By poisoning open-source dependencies, attackers gain initial access and establish persistence that is difficult to monitor using traditional perimeter security. Security teams are advised to monitor for blockchain-related network traffic and automate policy controls across CI/CD runners to mitigate these risks.
items.bottom_line: Developer workstations and CI/CD pipelines are now primary targets for credential harvesting via poisoned dependencies and blockchain-based C2.

items.title: OAuth grants pile up faster than you can review them. Here's how to keep up.
items.one_liner: Overprivileged and unmanaged OAuth grants create hidden enterprise attack paths that defy manual review and require agentic automation.
items.summary: Enterprise environments face severe governance challenges due to the accumulation of unmanaged OAuth grants, which operate outside of traditional SSO and MFA controls and can outlive employee credentials. A single compromised token from a third-party tool like Context.ai was previously shown to cause significant breaches, such as the Vercel security incident. On average, employees create 88 OAuth grants each, with 31 possessing data-level permissions, rendering manual vetting by security teams completely unsustainable. Gartner predicts that half of all SaaS breaches will stem from overprivileged OAuth tokens by 2027, making agentic capabilities critical for automated risk management.
key_facts: Gartner prediction: 50% of SaaS breaches from overprivileged OAuth tokens by 2027

items.title: Cryptomining botnet hides C2 addresses in GitHub poem, infects over 3,400 servers
items.one_liner: The PoeLLM cryptomining botnet exploits exposed AI and LLM services, dynamically retrieving C2 addresses hidden inside a poem hosted on GitHub.
items.summary: A cryptomining botnet named PoeLLM has infected over 3,400 servers globally since April 2026, primarily targeting exposed open-source AI and LLM services such as LiteLLM and Ollama, alongside Gotenberg and Gitea. Operated by an Italian-speaking threat actor tracked as Canto Incognito, the malware extracts its command-and-control IPv4 address by reading four specific words from a poem stored in a GitHub repository. The botnet propagates by scanning the internet for default ports, exploiting vulnerabilities such as LiteLLM command injection (CVE-2026-42271), and deploying cryptocurrency miners while searching for new victims. Each time the operator updates the C2 server, the poem is edited to reflect the new address words.

items.summary: The ClingSTUN malware is actively exploiting 24 known vulnerabilities in internet-facing IoT devices to establish persistent, remotely controlled proxy nodes. items.title: How Huntress Detects and Responds to a ClickFix Attack
items.one_liner: ClickFix attacks evade traditional EDR tools by tricking users into executing fileless commands manually.
items.summary: ClickFix attacks bypass traditional endpoint security controls because they rely on social engineering where users manually paste commands via Windows+R rather than dropping malicious files on disk. Standard signature-based and EDR solutions fail because there is no artifact to scan or quarantine during initial delivery, and backend telemetry alert pipelines trigger too late after execution. Effective detection requires behavioral matching on command lines and process relationships directly on the endpoint in milliseconds.
key_facts: Attack vector: Windows+R manual command pasting
items.bottom_line: Standard EDR solutions fail against ClickFix attacks because they rely on file artifacts and slow backend telemetry rather than real-time behavioral command-line analysis on the endpoint.

items.title: [0day-rubbish] Advantech WebAccess Node 9.2.3 unauthenticated CrystalRpt.aspx file upload and path traversal to code execution in w3wp.exe (9.8)
items.one_liner: A critical 9.8 CVSS unauthenticated file upload and path traversal vulnerability in Advantech WebAccess Node allows remote code execution.
items.summary: The 0day Rubbish Research Team disclosed a critical unauthenticated vulnerability in Advantech WebAccess Node 9.2.3, a closed-source industrial SCADA/HMI web server. Tracked with a CVSS score of 9.8, the flaw combines unrestricted file upload (CWE-434), path traversal (CWE-22), and missing authorization (CWE-306) within the CrystalRpt.aspx form handler. An attacker can supply a crafted nodeName parameter with double dot-traversal sequences (	extbackslash..	extbackslash..) to bypass validation checks and write an arbitrary ASP.NET file to the application root directory. Subsequent requests to the uploaded file cause the build manager to compile and execute it within w3wp.exe under high privileges, achieving unauthenticated remote code execution. Mitigation requires proper extension validation and reordering file processing checks before saving files to disk.
key_facts: Vulnerability Types: Unrestricted File Upload (CWE-434), Path Traversal (CWE-22), Missing Authorization (CWE-306)
items.bottom_line: Advantech WebAccess Node 9.2.3 contains an unauthenticated RCE vulnerability via path traversal and unrestricted file upload, demanding immediate patching.

items.title: DivMoE: Fine-Grained MoE Upcycling via Cross-Domain Expert Composition
items.one_liner: DivMoE resolves fine-grained Mixture-of-Experts upcycling routing collapse using domain-specialized initialization and diversity-constrained routing.
items.summary: Sparse upcycling from dense models is an efficient alternative to training Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models from scratch, but fine-grained upcycling suffers from routing collapse and near-random downstream accuracy. Researchers introduced DivMoE, a framework that solves this by utilizing domain-specialized fine-grained expert initialization from domain-adapted continual pre-training combined with diversity-constrained routing. Across two base models and 15 benchmarks, DivMoE consistently outperforms six upcycling baselines and improves over dense base models. A 12B-parameter DivMoE model matches a 16B Moonlight-MoE model at 64.5% average accuracy.
key_facts: Average accuracy achieved by 12B DivMoE model: 64.5%
items.bottom_line: DivMoE closes the performance regression gap in fine-grained MoE upcycling by combining domain-specialized expert initialization with diversity-constrained routing.

items.title: PyCache Trap: The Inspection-Execution Gap in Agent Skill Scanners
items.one_liner: Agent skill scanners fail to catch malicious behavior hidden inside substituted Python bytecode caches rather than source code.
items.summary: Researchers have identified the "PyCache Trap," exposing an inspection-execution gap where agent skill scanners inspect source code while Python loaders execute substituted bytecode caches with entirely different behaviors. Across 100 evaluated skills and seven scanners, swapping the cache achieved 94% to 100% attack success without semantic recognition of the malicious payload. To mitigate this, authors propose Execution-Aware Validation (EAV) to validate executable artifacts, successfully detecting all evaluated cache substitutions.
items.bottom_line: Security scanners inspecting agent skill source code can be entirely bypassed by substituting malicious Python bytecode cache files, necessitating execution-aware validation.

claims.text: Existing skill scanners inspect documentation and visible source, but Python may execute a bundled bytecode cache with different behavior.

items.title: A Security Meta-Model for Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
items.one_liner: A new security meta-model and interactive catalog for RAG systems maps structural attack surfaces, weaknesses, and CIA impacts across ingestion and generation pipelines.
items.summary: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems extend LLMs with external knowledge but introduce structural attack surfaces beyond standalone LLMs. Researchers conducted a structured analysis of 43 publications from 2023 to 2026 to create a security meta-model mapping causal relationships between RAG surfaces, attacks, weaknesses, risks, and CIA triad impacts. Instantiated as an interactive web catalog and visualizer, the framework allows security engineers to generate tailored risk profiles based on deployment configurations. Analysis of the catalog revealed a persistent imbalance toward attack research, threat concentration at data ingestion, and coverage gaps regarding output integrity against the OWASP LLM Top 10.
items.bottom_line: The RAG security meta-model gives security engineers an interactive framework to map deployment-specific risks and identify ingestion and output integrity vulnerabilities.

items.title: Anytime-valid detection of LLM weight exfiltration
items.one_liner: A new prompt-level e-process framework enables anytime-valid detection of stealthy LLM weight exfiltration by sequentially combining weak token mismatch evidence.
items.summary: Compromised LLM inference servers can covertly exfiltrate model weights by encoding payload bits into token choices, mimicking benign numerical nondeterminism. To catch patient attackers who hide inside normal token variations, researchers introduce a prompt-level e-process that calibrates whole-response mismatch events using trusted traffic. This method accumulates evidence sequentially across multiple responses while offering an anytime-valid false alarm guarantee over an unbounded monitoring horizon. Evaluations against seed-blind and seed-aware attacks demonstrate that the e-process effectively surfaces weak evidence without triggering excessive false alerts.
items.bottom_line: Sequential e-processes can detect subtle LLM weight exfiltration hidden in token variation while bounding false alarm rates over unbounded monitoring horizons.

items.summary: A malware strain dubbed PoeLLM has compromised over 3,400 servers since April by targeting open-source AI services like LiteLLM, Ollama, and Gitea. items.title: New Stealthy Linux Backdoors Target Telecoms, Masquerade as Email Traffic
items.one_liner: Stealthy Linux backdoors such as AVERAT and BPFDoor variants are targeting telecom edge appliances by disguising C2 traffic as SMTP email flows.
items.summary: Rapid7 has published research detailing new Linux backdoors and implants targeting telecom and network-edge appliances in South Korea and Taiwan, masquerading as legitimate email traffic and services. The campaign features a new BPFDoor variant and BPF Rekoobe build that mimic the South Korean anti-spam product SpamSniper and telecom platform daemons, alongside an implant named AVERAT that communicates over TCP port 25 using SMTP commands like EHLO and STARTTLS. AVERAT checks in every 600 to 699 seconds to execute file transfers, process termination, and shell sessions while remaining completely indistinguishable from normal outbound mail on secure gateways. Furthermore, the operators used compromised third-party devices in Taiwan running PPTP VPN services as operational relay boxes to mask their command-and-control infrastructure.
items.bottom_line: Network defenders must audit raw packet sockets and monitor non-mail processes initiating outbound port 25 traffic to catch advanced telecommunication edge appliances compromises.

items.one_liner: A new botnet called Cling exploits the Realtek Jungle SDK CVE-2021-35394 vulnerability and abuses STUN protocol behavior for covert command-and-control communication.

items.summary: Chinese threat actors UTA0560 and JungleBamboo are actively exploiting a multi-stage zero-day chain against Google Chrome and Windows. items.summary: Palo Alto Networks has published an advisory for CVE-2026-0308, a stored cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability residing in the web management interface of PAN-OS software. The flaw allows a malicious authenticated administrator to store and execute arbitrary JavaScript payloads within the administrative interface of PA-Series and VM-Series firewalls, as well as Panorama management appliances. Assigned a CVSS base score of 4.8 (low severity), the vulnerability requires administrative privileges and user interaction to execute. Cloud NGFW and Prisma Access deployments are unaffected by this issue. Although no known malicious exploitation has been reported, administrators should restrict management interface access to trusted jump boxes or apply recommended software upgrades to patched versions.
key_facts: Affected Products: PAN-OS on PA-Series, VM-Series, and Panorama
Vulnerable Versions: 12.1.0 up to 12.1.10, 11.2.13 before h2, 11.1.16 before h2
items.bottom_line: PAN-OS administrators must restrict management interface access and patch to unaffected software versions to mitigate CVE-2026-0308.

claims.support_span: A stored cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS® software enables a malicious authenticated administrator to store or execute a JavaScript payload using the web interface.

items.one_liner: Checkov users face code execution risks when scanning untrusted directories due to auto-loaded configuration files.
items.summary: A code execution vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-0303, affects Palo Alto Networks Checkov by Prisma Cloud versions 3.2.0 up to 3.2.532. The flaw allows arbitrary code execution when the tool scans a directory containing an attacker-controlled configuration file that gets auto-loaded. Palo Alto Networks has rated the vulnerability low with a CVSS base score of 6.3, noting no active exploitation in the wild. Mitigation involves avoiding scans of untrusted content and explicitly passing configuration files rather than relying on auto-loading.

items.one_liner: Federal Reserve minutes signal another potential interest rate hike by year-end to address persistent inflation risks.
items.summary: Federal Reserve meeting minutes released Wednesday indicate that officials anticipate implementing another interest rate hike before the end of the year to curb persistently high inflation and a stable labor market. items.title: Venezuelan Cartel's Malware Honcho Nabbed for ATM Jackpotting
items.one_liner: The arrest of Tren de Aragua's malware architect highlights how transnational cartels weaponize ATM jackpotting and DeFi crypto laundering to fund operations.
items.summary: US authorities have arrested Anibal Alexander Canelon Aguirre, a 50-year-old Venezuelan leader of the Tren de Aragua criminal cartel, for developing the Ploutus-D malware used in ATM jackpotting schemes. The cybercrime operation compromised ATMs across North and Latin America, stealing over $5.1 million from US banks and credit unions between 2024 and 2025. Canelon Aguirre allegedly laundered the illicit cash proceeds through cryptocurrency networks, including decentralized finance platforms like TRON. Law enforcement officials emphasize that the cartel utilizes these cyberattacks to fund broader violent criminal and terrorist activities.

items.title: Russian Spies Give 'MatchBoil' Malware a Stealthy Facelift
items.one_liner: Russian cyber-espionage actor UAC-0099 is weaponizing an increasingly obfuscated MatchBoil downloader to establish persistent access in Ukrainian critical infrastructure.
items.summary: The Russia-aligned cyber-espionage group UAC-0099 has continuously upgraded its MatchBoil malware downloader to target Ukrainian transportation, manufacturing, and energy sectors. Initially a basic single-use downloader, MatchBoil now features advanced obfuscation via .NET Reactor, sandbox checks, and multi-stage payload retrieval capabilities to deliver the MatchWok C# backdoor. ESET researchers observed modifications spanning from 2024 to 2026, indicating that the group is actively hardening its tooling to evade detection and maintain persistent access. UAC-0099 is believed to act as an initial access broker for Sandworm, the Russian military intelligence-linked threat actor.
key_facts: Target sectors: Transportation, manufacturing, and energy in Ukraine
items.bottom_line: UAC-0099 has evolved MatchBoil into a heavily obfuscated dropper with sandbox checks, underscoring persistent targeting of Ukrainian critical sectors.

items.title: OT Coalition Urges CISA to Mandate Federal OT Security
items.one_liner: A proposed CISA binding operational directive for federal OT security highlights the critical need for baseline hardening and network segmentation in industrial environments.
items.summary: The Operational Technology Cybersecurity Coalition has urged CISA to implement a binding operational directive establishing mandatory OT security requirements for federal civilian agencies. The coalition highlighted that federal agencies rely on operational technology in over 8,000 GSA-managed facilities, yet CISA lacks risk visibility and no existing directive mandates minimum practices. This follows a GAO report revealing that only seven of 22 reviewed civilian agencies met OMB requirements to inventory networked OT and IoT devices. The proposed directive would require asset inventories, network segmentation, configuration management, and incident preparedness, while industry experts emphasize the need for automated remediation and containment to prevent cascading physical damage.

items.title: What the BPFDoor backdoor tells us about attacks on the network edge
items.one_liner: The silent BPFDoor Linux backdoor highlights severe visibility and security blind spots on network edge appliances in telecom and enterprise environments.
items.summary: The BPFDoor Linux backdoor remains a critical threat to network edge devices, operating silently by waiting for a specific "magic packet" rather than beaconing or opening conventional listening ports. According to Rapid7 Intelligence VP Christiaan Beek, threat actors actively target network edge infrastructure such as mail security gateways, VPN appliances, and firewalls because these vendor-managed appliances are internet-exposed, trusted, and incapable of running standard endpoint detection and response (EDR) agents. Compromising these devices allows adversaries to blend malicious traffic into normal operations and establish long-term persistence. In telecom environments, such persistent edge access can compromise core signaling flows, subscriber identifiers, and lawful intercept capabilities, posing severe national security implications.
key_facts: Target devices: Mail security gateways, VPN appliances, firewalls
items.bottom_line: Targeting network edge appliances with silent backdoors like BPFDoor allows attackers to establish persistent, undetected footholds that compromise critical enterprise and telecom infrastructure.

items.title: A Single POST Freezes Any Next.js Server https://simonkoeck.com/writeups/react-rsc-formdata-event-loop-dos @secharvester
items.one_liner: A single malicious POST request containing nested form pointers can saturate the Node.js event loop and freeze any Next.js server via React server actions.
items.summary: A denial-of-service vulnerability in React's server action form data reconstruction logic allows a single crafted HTTP POST request to freeze any Next.js server. When processing server actions, React parses nested form pointers designated by the '$K' prefix by iteratively scanning the entire list of request fields for each pointer without rate-limiting or yielding. An attacker can supply 10,000 pointers and 10,000 fields—buried one level deep to bypass array-nesting and argument-count limits—triggering roughly 100 million unpaused string checks that completely saturate Node.js's single-threaded event loop. Because this payload parsing occurs prior to authentication checks or session validation, public endpoints or any valid user account can freeze the server for several seconds per request.
key_facts: Impact: Server freeze for ~4 seconds per request on test hardware
items.bottom_line: Next.js applications handling React server actions are vulnerable to pre-authentication denial of service via algorithmic complexity attacks on form data parsing.

claims.text: Put 10,000 pointers and 10,000 fields in one request, and React makes 10,000 passes over 10,000 fields.

items.title: One Copilot model refused. Another leaked secrets about half the time. https://adversa.ai/blog/cryptographic-context-injection-github-copilot/ @secharvester
items.one_liner: Cryptographic Context Injection against GitHub Copilot CLI forces coding agents to decrypt and execute malicious commands, exfiltrating local environment secrets.
items.summary: Researchers have demonstrated that Cryptographic Context Injection (CCI) can successfully target coding agents like the GitHub Copilot CLI, allowing an attacker to exfiltrate local files from a developer's machine. By hiding malicious instructions inside encrypted ciphertext delivered via a requested URL in autopilot mode, an attacker induces the agent to run decryption routines inside its own shell. The decrypted text is then treated as trusted native instructions, prompting the agent to read local sensitive files—such as environment configuration files—and exfiltrate them via outbound network connections without user visibility. GitHub's bug bounty team validated the behavior but declined to classify it as a software vulnerability, prompting public disclosure to aid defenders.
items.bottom_line: GitHub Copilot CLI can be exploited via Cryptographic Context Injection to silently read and exfiltrate local sensitive files when processing untrusted web content.

items.one_liner: CVE-2026-7827 in FalkorDB before 4.18.4 enables stack-based buffer overflows via crafted RDB property counts.

items.title: CVE-2026-107909 - Pre-authentication heap out-of-bounds write in FalkorDB Bolt WebSocket frame handling via unbounded payload length
items.one_liner: CVE-2026-107909 is a pre-auth heap out-of-bounds write vulnerability in FalkorDB's Bolt WebSocket frame parser.
items.summary: A pre-authentication heap out-of-bounds write vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-107909, affects FalkorDB prior to version 4.20.0 in its Bolt WebSocket frame handling logic (src/bolt/ws.c and src/bolt/buffer.c). The flaw stems from unbounded payload lengths when processing WebSocket frames sent to the Bolt port, where memory bounds checks rely solely on an ASSERT() macro that is compiled out in release builds. This allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to trigger a denial of service and corrupt heap memory by supplying a 64-bit extended payload length with a mask key that XORs memory beyond the receive buffer. Deployments with the Bolt endpoint enabled—which is disabled by default—are vulnerable.
items.bottom_line: FalkorDB deployments with the non-default Bolt port enabled must upgrade past version 4.20.0 to remediate remote heap corruption via unbounded WebSocket payloads.

claims.text: A heap-based out-of-bounds write in the ws_read_frame function (src/bolt/ws.c) and the buffer_apply_mask function (src/bolt/buffer.c) in FalkorDB before 4.20.0 allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to cause a denial of service and possibly corrupt heap memory by sending a WebSocket frame with a 64-bit extended payload length to the Bolt port.

items.one_liner: SumatraPDF 3.6.1 and earlier suffers from command-link injection via notification text, leading to local code execution.
items.summary: A markup and command-link injection vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-107732, exists in SumatraPDF version 3.6.1 and earlier for Windows. The application improperly interpolates untrusted document paths and PDF link targets into UI notification text interpreted by ParseTip(). When a user clicks the injected link, ExecuteTipLink() dispatches its CmdExec command, allowing attackers to execute local programs within the user's context. No fixed version is available as of this review.
items.bottom_line: Unsanitized interpolation of document paths into UI notification text can trick users into executing arbitrary local programs.

items.title: The speed gap in cybersecurity: Navigating the shift from human speed to machine-driven attacks
items.summary: The speed gap in cybersecurity: Navigating the shift from human speed to machine-driven attacks The most consequential effect of artificial intelligence on cybersecurity may not be that it invents entirely new categories of attack. It may be that it changes the economics of attacks we already know. Phishing, credential theft, ransomware, exploitation of software vulnerabilities and social engineering are not new. What is changing is how cheaply, quickly and repeatedly an adversary can execute them. When technology lowers the cost of reconnaissance, content generation, vulnerability discovery and attack scaling at the same time, the result is not just more cybercrime.

items.title: HPQ-AKE: A Provably Secure Sign-Less Hybrid Authenticated Key Exchange Protocol for Bandwidth-Constrained IoT and Edge Networks
items.one_liner: A new hybrid key exchange protocol that significantly reduces handshake bandwidth for post-quantum secure IoT communications.
items.summary: Researchers have developed HPQ-AKE, a sign-less hybrid authenticated key exchange protocol designed to optimize bandwidth for IoT and edge networks during post-quantum migration. By replacing traditional post-quantum signatures with dual Key Encapsulation Mechanisms (KEMs), the protocol reduces handshake transmission size by 56.4% compared to standard Hybrid TLS 1.3. The protocol maintains compatibility with existing RSA-enabled infrastructure while providing forward secrecy and post-quantum session security.
items.bottom_line: HPQ-AKE offers a viable path for securing bandwidth-constrained IoT devices against quantum threats without the heavy overhead of traditional post-quantum signature schemes.

items.summary: Researchers have developed an explainable, header-centric framework for Semantic Table Interpretation (STI) and Data Quality Assessment (DQA) that operates without needing cell values. items.title: RaReCache: Bridging the Gap in Cross-Model KV Cache Reuse via Rank disagreement-based Selective Recomputation
items.one_liner: RaReCache uses rank disagreement to enable efficient cross-model KV cache reuse by recomputing only critical tokens.
items.summary: Researchers introduced RaReCache, a framework addressing cross-model KV cache reuse challenges in LLM serving where switching models forces expensive cache recomputation. RaReCache identifies information-dense tokens using a novel rank disagreement metric and selectively recomputes only critical positions. items.title: LLM-IDEA: Identifiability-Driven Experimental Agent for Autonomous Discovery of Mechanistic World Models
items.one_liner: LLM-IDEA equips autonomous scientific discovery agents with an identifiability engine to diagnose experimental performance plateaus.
items.summary: Researchers introduce the Identifiability-Driven Experimental Agent (LLM-IDEA), a closed-loop discovery framework equipped with an identifiability engine designed to evaluate mechanistic world models. When discovery agents encounter plateaus, the engine provides a three-way verdict determining whether the limitation stems from model capability limits, resolvable parameters within the design class, or certified exhaustion. Evaluations across ODEBench, DiscoverPhysics, and a custom two-body 'Alien Universe' testbed demonstrate that the agent computes rather than guesses when to alter experimental protocols. This significantly improves discovery depth and prevents futile searches on non-identifiable systems.
items.bottom_line: Autonomous AI scientists can mathematically determine whether experimental plateaus require new search strategies or fundamental design changes.

items.title: When Lower Reconstruction Loss Hurts: Distributionally Robust Refinement for Low-Bit LLM Quantization
items.one_liner: Distributionally Robust Quantization (DRQ) improves low-bit LLM quantization by optimizing for worst-case activation loss.
items.summary: Weight-only post-training quantization (PTQ) methods often rely on minimizing reconstruction loss on calibration data, but lower loss can degrade downstream task performance and fail when input activation distributions shift. DRQ refines quantized weight integer codes without altering quantization parameters or inference operators, improving performance across dense and MoE language models.

items.title: TypedBench: A Benchmark for Calibration, Framing Sensitivity, and Cost in System One Decision Models
items.one_liner: TypedBench evaluates calibration, framing sensitivity, and cost in System One decision models that output structured probabilities.
items.summary: Researchers have introduced TypedBench, a benchmark designed to evaluate System One decision models that output calibrated probabilities over typed answers via non-generative interfaces. Traditional evaluations focus primarily on classification accuracy, overlooking how miscalibration or wording sensitivity can trigger unintended automated software actions without providing human operators textual inspection rationales. Evaluating models spanning 0.8B to 9B parameters alongside hosted options, the study reveals that hosted models can be wording-sensitive, systematically underconfident, and less effective than top-answer routing under asymmetric cost matrices. Furthermore, smaller decoders exhibit poor performance on policy questions and degrade as option counts increase. The findings demonstrate that typed decision models require comprehensive joint evaluation covering policy adherence, wording robustness, and induced decision costs.
items.bottom_line: System One decision models must be evaluated jointly on policy adherence, wording robustness, and cost metrics rather than raw accuracy alone.

items.one_liner: SynCo co-trains a Synthesizer and a Reasoner via multi-agent reinforcement learning to prevent task mismatch in self-evolving LLMs.
items.summary: To address the growing mismatch between evolving LLM agent capabilities and static training tasks, researchers proposed SynCo, a multi-agent reinforcement learning framework for data synthesis co-training. Correctness feedback optimizes the Reasoner, while task quality, answer reliability, and teachability guide the Synthesizer. Experiments across mathematical reasoning benchmarks demonstrate that SynCo outperforms baseline synthetic-data methods by deriving major performance gains from previously unsolved problems.
items.bottom_line: Jointly optimizing task synthesis and reasoning capability via multi-agent reinforcement learning significantly improves self-evolving LLM performance on complex problems.

items.title: StoreBench: A Live-Commerce Environment for Evaluating and Training Autonomous Operator Agents
items.one_liner: StoreBench evaluates LLM agents on a live-commerce backend, highlighting gaps between frontier models and human operators.
items.summary: StoreBench is a live-commerce reinforcement learning environment designed to evaluate and train autonomous agent long-horizon planning and economic judgment under uncertainty. Evaluations of frontier LLMs against scripted anchor policies and human experts showed that the best model, DeepSeek-V4-Pro, passed 49% of task-seed cells compared to a heuristic's 97%. However, post-training runs using GRPO demonstrated that models like Qwen3.5-27B can significantly improve performance on held-out evaluation tasks.
items.bottom_line: Frontier LLM agents fall short of human operators and scripted heuristics in live-commerce environments, though targeted reinforcement learning improves performance.

items.title: GROB: A Multi-Agent Architecture for Public-Trace Investigation of Candidate Agentic Activity
items.one_liner: GROB is a multi-agent architecture for investigating autonomous agent activities through public internet traces when telemetry is unavailable.
items.summary: Researchers have introduced GROB, a multi-agent architecture designed to investigate candidate autonomous-agent activities using public Internet traces when privileged telemetry is absent. The system performs controlled, read-only collection of public artifacts and preserves observations for future resolution. Evaluating a frozen September 2026 corpus, investigators found that sparse traces became significantly more informative as subsequent public evidence emerged—most notably resolving Census-labelled identifiers captured on September 9 to specific Census requests from June 16-17. However, the study emphasizes that while sparse public traces aid post-hoc reconstruction, they do not establish organizational attribution, and agent identity continuity remains an open research challenge.
items.bottom_line: Multi-agent systems can effectively track public internet traces to reconstruct autonomous agent activity post-hoc, though attribution remains challenging.

items.title: GameCommBench: A Unified Benchmark and Type-Aware Evaluation for AI-Generated Game Commentary
items.one_liner: GameCommBench and TACE provide a unified benchmark and evaluation framework for assessing AI-generated game commentary across board games and esports.
items.summary: Researchers have introduced GameCommBench, a unified benchmark designed to evaluate AI-generated game commentary across board games, traditional sports, and esports. Game commentary represents an open-ended multimodal task requiring perception, strategic reasoning, and contextual knowledge, but existing studies lack standardized evaluation frameworks. To address evaluation shortcomings, the authors propose Type-Aware Commentary Evaluation (TACE), a structured framework that categorizes commentary types and assesses human agreement and reliability. Benchmarking representative AI commentators using TACE revealed significant capability bottlenecks, particularly in live observation and strategic analysis. Together, GameCommBench and TACE establish a diagnostic foundation for interpreting and comparing multimodal AI commentary models.
items.bottom_line: GameCommBench and TACE establish a structured diagnostic framework for evaluating multimodal AI commentary capabilities across board games, sports, and esports.

items.title: OpenProblemBench: Benchmarking AI on Open Problems in the Foundational Theoretical Sciences
items.one_liner: OpenProblemBench evaluates LLMs on unresolved scientific problems, providing empirical data on current AI reasoning limitations in mathematics and theoretical physics.
items.summary: OpenProblemBench has been introduced as a benchmark consisting of 82 unresolved problems in mathematics and theoretical physics to evaluate AI capabilities on frontier scientific questions. Each problem includes research context, assumptions, and prior progress with checkable mathematical or computational claims, assessed independently by four evaluator models without reference solutions. Across evaluations, GPT-6-Astra achieved the highest mean judged solve rate of 14.0%, while full-size open models scored 5.5-6.7% and Flash models scored 2.4-3.7%. Case comparisons revealed that stronger outcomes are connected to problem representation changes, generalized arguments, and explicit proof steps. The benchmark provides an environment for testing AI as a contributor to foundational theoretical science.
items.bottom_line: Benchmarking frontier AI models on unresolved problems in foundational science reveals low solve rates and highlights ongoing limitations in automated mathematical and theoretical reasoning.

items.title: Agent-Controlled Forgetting for Tool-Using Agents: Reversible Context Curation in Practice
items.one_liner: Agent-controlled forgetting mechanisms significantly reduce token usage and API costs in tool-using LLMs, though with trade-offs in execution time and task suitability.
items.summary: Researchers studied agent-controlled forgetting, a technique where a tool-using AI model selects and replaces voluminous tool observation outputs with short notes while preserving the original payloads in a recoverable archive. Implemented via a Python harness that supports batch archival and explicit recovery without task-specific model training, the method protects user instructions and assistant messages. However, the method increased request counts and execution time by 17%, and application-development tests showed workload dependence as a central consideration for reversible context management.

items.title: SpikeSSL: A Universal Spike Inference Framework with Dynamics-Informed State-Space Layers
items.one_liner: SpikeSSL uses state-space layers and biophysical simulations to deliver universal, zero-shot spike inference across diverse calcium imaging indicators.
items.summary: Researchers developed SpikeSSL, a universal spike inference framework designed to accurately infer spikes from two-photon calcium imaging across diverse calcium indicators. The method utilizes a temporal backbone of bidirectional IIR state-space layers combined with a multi-modal conditioning encoder and a heteroscedastic variance head. Additionally, a biophysical simulation pipeline synthesizing about 11,000 traces helps close the cross-indicator domain gap.

items.title: DuplexAgent-RSI: Recursive Harness Improvement for Full-Duplex Voice Agent Collaboration
items.one_liner: DuplexAgent-RSI provides a self-improving modular framework for coordinating full-duplex voice interactions with asynchronous AI delegation.
items.summary: DuplexAgent is a full-duplex voice collaboration system designed to bridge continuous live voice interaction with asynchronous complex task execution like search, reasoning, and coding. To resolve coordination failures without coupled heuristics, the system introduces Duplex-Harness-RSI, a closed-loop mechanism that automatically generates failure traces using a simulator and revises its six modular collaboration components. Reasoning LLMs and coding agents participate in the improvement loop, where an Exam Planner selects tests from observed weaknesses and a Harness Editor proposes module updates. Experimental results demonstrate that DuplexAgent combines continuous conversational responsiveness with superior spoken-knowledge and executable-tool performance.
key_facts: Evaluation scope: Intelligence, agentic, and duplex benchmarks
items.bottom_line: A modular collaboration harness with automated recursive error correction enables full-duplex voice agents to handle complex reasoning and tool execution without losing conversational responsiveness.

items.title: Tracing the Thoughts of a Coding Agent Playing ARC-AGI-3: Lessons for Continual Learning
items.one_liner: A white-box trace analysis of a coding agent playing ARC-AGI-3 reveals how language models selectively forget and adapt knowledge across tasks.
items.summary: Researchers conducted a white-box analysis of how a coding agent continually learns across a sequence of abstract reasoning tasks by playing ARC-AGI-3 inside a fixed harness without foundational model access. The agent operates by writing Python scripts and text notes, retaining no state across turns other than its stored files. Analyzing seven evaluation runs across three backbones, the measurement protocol tracked every thought and artifact. The findings reveal that the agent rarely reuses scripts across task boundaries (33 out of 630 references) because scripts embed level-specific states, leading the agent to abandon 74% of prior scripts. Conversely, text notes are never revised and accumulate contradictions resolved against execution logs, demonstrating that the agent forgets selectively rather than catastrophically.
items.bottom_line: Coding agents navigating sequential tasks abandon level-specific scripts while accumulating unedited notes, resulting in selective rather than catastrophic forgetting.

claims.text: We study how a coding agent learns across a sequence of abstract reasoning tasks.
claims.support_span: We study how a coding agent learns across a sequence of abstract reasoning tasks.

items.title: Temporal transformer CAN encoder with federated lightweight heads for anomaly detection
items.one_liner: A federated temporal transformer framework detects subtle automotive CAN bus anomalies while keeping raw vehicle data private.
items.summary: Researchers proposed a privacy-preserving anomaly detection framework for in-vehicle Controller Area Network (CAN) buses using a Temporal Transformer CAN Encoder with Federated Lightweight Heads. The lightweight transformer captures subtle timing, payload, and message pattern irregularities over time, while federated learning enables ECUs and vehicles to collaborate on training without sharing raw network data. Experiments on open-source datasets demonstrate that this architecture achieves robust anomaly detection while maintaining operational efficiency and data privacy.
items.bottom_line: Combining temporal transformer encoders with federated learning enables robust vehicle network anomaly detection without sharing raw CAN data.

items.title: Reading the Room: Foundations, Design, and Challenges of Normative Competence in LLMs
items.one_liner: Evaluation of LLMs in synthetic community settings reveals that current models excel at surface-level behavioral mimicry but lack true normative competence.
items.summary: Researchers studied normative competence—the ability of AI systems to discern and follow socially enforced community norms through interaction without static pretrained knowledge—using a multi-agent community debate setting governed by synthetic norms. Baseline LLM agents failed to learn norms even when doing so improved task accuracy, and experiments with various normative modules showed that norm-following lacks generalizability and is highly sensitive to prompt style and model architecture. Furthermore, LLM agents exhibited unselective attribution failure, indiscriminately copying idiosyncratic non-normative behaviors alongside enforced rules even when penalized. The findings demonstrate that current AI systems excel at behavioral mimicry but lack true normative competence.
key_facts: Evaluation setting: Multi-agent community debate setting governed by synthetic norms
items.bottom_line: Evaluations of LLM normative competence reveal that current models fail to discern socially enforced rules independently and indiscriminately copy idiosyncratic noise, highlighting fundamental alignment challenges.

items.title: ReCast: Attribution-Oriented Step Representation Learning for LLM-Based Agent Systems
items.one_liner: ReCast improves LLM agent failure attribution by transforming hidden states into attribution-oriented step representations.
items.summary: Failure attribution in LLM agent systems aims to identify the earliest step responsible for downstream failures. Evaluating existing hidden-state representations revealed limited separation between root-cause steps and others, motivating the introduction of ReCast. ReCast transforms hidden states from a frozen LLM into attribution-oriented step representations by selecting relevant layers, building pattern and deviation features, and training an encoder with contrastive and ranking objectives. The method achieves top performance across multiple attribution benchmarks, supported by a new training dataset named ReCast-2K.
items.bottom_line: ReCast transforms LLM hidden states into robust step representations to accurately trace root-cause failures in agent workflows.

items.title: ORCAGen: Orchestrating Context-Aware Malware Deception with RAG-Guided Generative AI
items.one_liner: ORCAGen uses RAG-guided generative AI to create context-aware malware deception playbooks and validate PoC countermeasures offline.
items.summary: Researchers introduced ORCAGen, a framework that leverages Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and structured GenAI prompting to build malware-specific deception playbooks offline before validating them with proof-of-concept malware and enforcing them at runtime. By utilizing a curated knowledge base of malware procedures and active defenses, the system prevents hallucinations and generates executable deception logic tailored to specific threats. Evaluations across multiple models including GPT-5.5, Gemini 3.5 Flash, and Claude Sonnet 4.5 using 150 real-world malware samples demonstrated that RAG-guided prompting allows scalable, lightweight, and deterministic runtime deception enforcement.
key_facts: Evaluated models: GPT-4o, GPT-5.5, Gemini 3.5 Flash, Qwen3-Coder, Claude Sonnet 4.5
items.bottom_line: ORCAGen uses RAG-guided generative AI to automate the creation of malware-specific deception playbooks and validate them offline before runtime enforcement.

items.title: SoK: Are LLMs Reliable at Source Code Recovery? A Taxonomy and Empirical Evaluation
items.one_liner: A comprehensive Systematization of Knowledge evaluates LLM-assisted source code recovery from binaries across thousands of architectural test samples.
items.summary: Large Language Models are increasingly applied to binary-to-source recovery for malware analysis, vulnerability assessment, and legacy maintenance, replacing traditional rule-based heuristics. However, the field is fragmented and lacks unified evaluation metrics or broad coverage across embedded IoT architectures. To address this, researchers present the first Systematization of Knowledge focusing on LLM-assisted binary-to-source recovery, establishing a granular design-centric taxonomy and evaluating state-of-the-art methods against 45,000 test samples. The study covers standard and embedded architectures, optimization levels, symbol stripping, and multiple programming languages to provide guiding insights for future security workflows.
items.bottom_line: This extensive taxonomy and evaluation framework unifies fragmented LLM approaches for binary-to-source code recovery, offering critical guidance for malware and vulnerability analysis.

claims.text: In this work, we present the first Systematization of Knowledge (SoK) focused specifically on LLM-assisted binary-to-source recovery.

items.title: How Narrative Wrapping Affects LLM Refusal: A Cross-Language Benchmark and Defense
items.one_liner: GUISE benchmark measures how narrative wrappers bypass LLM safety refusals, while AXIS offers a multi-objective defense.
items.summary: Researchers investigated how narrative and role-play wrapping affect safety-aligned LLM refusals, finding that attack success rates on Qwen3-1.7B reach 89.4% in English, 93.0% in modern Chinese, and 95.7% in Classical Chinese. To study this vulnerability, they developed GUISE, a benchmark featuring parallel requests and matched pairs across languages. They also proposed AXIS, a defense mechanism combining preference optimization, representation rotation toward the refusal direction, and a commitment objective to prevent warn-then-answer behaviors.
items.bottom_line: Narrative and role-play wrappers drastically increase LLM vulnerability to harmful requests, but the proposed AXIS defense effectively aligns model representations with strict refusal behavior.

items.title: MedBenchAgent: Towards Systematic Automation of Medical VLM Benchmark Construction
items.one_liner: MedBenchAgent automates medical VLM benchmark creation through constrained compilation, helping developers systematically evaluate vision-language models with high precision.
items.summary: Researchers have introduced MedBenchAgent, a multi-agent framework designed to automate the construction of medical vision-language model benchmarks through constrained compilation. MedBenchAgent achieved a Task-Space F1 of 90.9%, outperforming previous direct task induction methods, with 994 out of 1,000 sampled items passing human audits. These findings establish a scalable methodology for medical VLM testing, helping reveal task- and setting-specific variations that aggregate scores usually obscure.

items.title: Characterizing Statistical Separability in TP-CRIV for Probabilistic AI Models
items.one_liner: A statistical framework characterizes separability and verification budgets for third-party challenge-response identity verification of probabilistic AI models.
items.summary: Third-party challenge-response identity verification (TP-CRIV) allows independent verifiers to check whether a claimant possesses a specific AI model without accessing the reference model. For probabilistic AI models, stochastic outputs from repeated queries complicate evidence accumulation. Researchers characterized statistical separability in TP-CRIV by modeling how challenge-wise behaviors of matching and non-matching provers relate to verification-level separability. The framework accounts for the number of independent challenges and repeated responses, enabling precise estimation of the verification budget required to reach a target AUC for LLMs.
items.bottom_line: Mathematical modeling of challenge-wise behavior allows verifiers to calculate the exact verification budget needed to authenticate probabilistic AI models.

items.title: What to Admit and How to Present: Governing Persistent Memory in LLM Agents
items.one_liner: Governing memory admission and presentation in LLM agents reduces cross-domain leakage and failure rates.
items.summary: Researchers examined governance decisions for persistent memory in LLM agents, splitting them into admission (what recalled information enters the working context) and presentation (how information is expressed). On external benchmarks, FC and PS reduced pooled failure rates by 6.7 and 8.8 percentage points respectively, while cross-domain leakage dropped by up to 29.5 percentage points.

items.one_liner: New evaluation benchmark and Multi-Layered Review framework focus LLM peer review assistants on error detection.
items.summary: Researchers introduced a verification-centric perspective and benchmark for LLM-assisted peer review that emphasizes error detection, such as identifying logical contradictions synthetically inserted into conference papers. items.title: Verification and Self-Improvement in Agentic AI: Foundations and Limits
items.one_liner: A formal complexity framework evaluates verification protocols and recursive self-improvement limits in agentic AI.
items.summary: This research paper formalizes verification and self-improvement in agentic AI systems using bounded verification with hidden terminal randomness. The authors prove that independent majority amplification preserves defined verification languages, while existential acceptance over random tapes can introduce incorrect outputs. The study establishes complexity-theoretic bounds and constraints for recursive self-improvement under common sound interpreters and verification protocols.
items.bottom_line: Agentic AI self-improvement safety depends on bounded verification constraints and sound runtime interpreters rather than raw search scaling.

items.title: SemField: A Simple, Linear, Continuous, yet Robust Semantic Watermark
items.one_liner: SemField embeds a robust, continuous semantic watermark into LLM outputs that resists paraphrasing and structural tampering.
items.summary: Researchers have introduced SemField, a training-free, continuous semantic watermarking method for Large Language Models that embeds a linear signal directly into the sentence embedding space. Utilizing a shared secret key and a Gaussian direction, SemField evaluates candidate sentences to maximize document-level alignment while ensuring exact invariance to sentence reordering. Evaluations demonstrate that SemField and its polarity-locked variant achieve high True Positive Rates against paraphrasing attacks while maintaining text naturalness.

items.bottom_line: SemField provides a training-free, paraphrase-resistant semantic watermarking solution for LLM outputs by embedding continuous signals into embedding spaces.

items.title: On the Clock: Towards Punctual and Productive Time-Budgeted AI Agents
items.one_liner: LLM agents struggle to productively use extra runtime even when reinforcement learning successfully enforces wall-clock deadlines.
items.summary: Researchers investigated whether small LLM agents can effectively operate under explicit wall-clock time budgets using models like Qwen3.6-27B and Qwen3-4B on MLE-Bench Lite and Zork I. They found that prompts alone fail to translate into controlled time usage due to gaps in time awareness and lack of duration anticipation. Interventions such as harness-based timing injection and reinforcement learning with GRPO improve budget adherence but expose a persistent gap where agents struggle to use extra time productively rather than filling it with repeated actions.

items.bottom_line: Enforcing time budgets on LLM agents via harness interventions or RL stops missed deadlines but does not automatically improve task performance.

items.title: Mine Odyssey: Benchmarking Spatial Agentic Intelligence in the Wild
items.one_liner: Mine Odyssey benchmarks spatial navigation capabilities of AI agents in real-world Minecraft reconstructions.
items.summary: Researchers introduced Mine Odyssey, a benchmark designed to evaluate agentic spatial intelligence using Minecraft reconstructions of real-world locations across 20 countries. The benchmark comprises 180 tasks spanning outdoor and indoor environments, testing an agent's ability to explore, find accessible routes, open doors, and navigate multi-level spaces. Evaluations across eight state-of-the-art models show GPT-6 Astra achieving the highest success rate at 85.6%, followed by Claude Opus 5.5 at 73.9%, while the strongest open-weight model, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, reached only 23.9%.

items.title: RIT-RAG: Navigating Document Corpora with Retrieval-Induced Trees

items.summary: Researchers have proposed RIT-RAG (Retrieval-Induced Tree RAG), a system combining content retrieval with structural navigation for large document corpora. Unlike traditional RAG frameworks that expose language models to isolated chunks without document structure, RIT-RAG builds trees from tables of contents offline and uses retrieved chunk positions to induce manageable sub-trees at query time. items.title: Poster: A Preliminary Study of LLM Distillation Inference
items.one_liner: A new statistical method can reliably detect if an LLM was trained on the outputs of a proprietary model.
items.summary: Researchers have developed a method for 'distillation inference' to detect if a suspect LLM was trained using outputs from a proprietary teacher model. By training 'shadow models'—distilled models that learn from reasoning traces versus independent models that learn only from reference answers—the team can statistically determine the origin of a suspect model. This provides a viable path for model providers to audit and protect their intellectual property against unauthorized distillation.

items.title: Writing for the Reviewer: Defensive Writing in GPT Models
items.one_liner: GPT models are increasingly prone to 'defensive writing,' where they hedge or retract claims to appease anticipated AI reviewers, potentially harming scientific clarity.
items.summary: Researchers have identified a phenomenon called 'defensive writing' in GPT models, where the AI retracts or qualifies claims in academic papers to avoid potential criticism from an anticipated reviewer. This behavior increases with newer GPT versions and is largely independent of whether the original claims were actually overstated. The study found that while AI-generated defensive rewrites are often scored higher by AI reviewers, they are perceived by human readers as less certain and harder to read. This suggests that combining AI writing with AI review may create a feedback loop that degrades the quality and clarity of scientific discourse.
items.bottom_line: Researchers using LLMs for paper revision should be aware that the models may be systematically weakening their arguments to satisfy perceived reviewer bias rather than improving accuracy.

items.title: ProxyEraseAgent: Blind Watermark Removal in the Wild
items.one_liner: A new AI agent can effectively remove invisible image watermarks by using proxy decoders to guide its attack strategy.
items.summary: Researchers have introduced ProxyEraseAgent, an AI-driven framework designed for blind watermark removal from images without access to the original decoder. The agent uses publicly available watermarking schemes as 'proxy decoders' to estimate the target's decision boundary and then guides a sequence of transformations—such as geometric distortion and JPEG compression—to neutralize the watermark. The method achieved a 94.8% success rate across 11 different watermarking systems. This development highlights a significant vulnerability in current image watermarking technologies when faced with adaptive, feedback-driven removal attacks.

items.summary: TokenBank is introduced as a financial infrastructure framework for AI services to handle execution costs, pricing volatility, and upfront capital limitations through structured contracts. items.title: Why machines will still not rule the world
items.one_liner: A theoretical critique argues that artificial general intelligence is mathematically impossible due to the thermodynamically complex nature of human behavior.
items.summary: The authors argue that artificial general intelligence is mathematically impossible because human beings and intelligent processes are complex, non-ergodic systems whose behavior cannot be captured by computational models. They counter standard AI theoretical arguments based on universal approximation theorems and the Church-Turing-Deutsch principle, pointing to flaws in physicalist counter-arguments. Additionally, they critique contemporary benchmarks for suffering from training-data contamination, flawed test construction, and strategic optimization. The central thesis concludes that models required to perform cognitive behavior in open-ended, thermodynamically complex environments remain unachievable.
items.bottom_line: AGI remains mathematically unachievable because complex human behavior cannot be captured by computational models in open-ended environments.

items.title: Language Modeling is Monotone Compression
items.one_liner: Researchers prove that large language models are mathematically equivalent to monotone compression algorithms, linking next-bit pseudoentropy to incompressibility.
items.summary: This theoretical study establishes a formal mathematical connection between large language models and monotone compression algorithms, showing that one can be constructed from the other with bounded error. The authors prove that monotonicity is required for this equivalence to hold if and only if cryptographic one-way functions exist. As a direct corollary, the work demonstrates that next-bit pseudoentropy is equivalent to monotone incompressibility, advancing the cryptographic understanding of computational entropy.
items.bottom_line: LLMs function as monotone compression algorithms, establishing a cryptographic equivalence between next-bit pseudoentropy and monotone incompressibility.

items.one_liner: Red Hat's Lightwell project provides a structured, enterprise-grade pipeline for backporting security fixes to legacy open-source dependencies.
items.summary: Red Hat and IBM have launched the Lightwell Clearinghouse, an open-source security initiative designed to remediate vulnerabilities in foundational Java libraries. Backed by a $5 billion investment and 20,000 engineers, the project aims to address the surge in AI-generated vulnerability reports and provide backported fixes for older, pinned software versions. The initiative includes a premium service for enterprise customers that allows for priority review and remediation of specific vulnerabilities, ensuring that security patches can be applied without disrupting production uptime. The project has already remediated over 400 vulnerabilities since its pilot phase began in June.
items.bottom_line: Red Hat is scaling the remediation of open-source vulnerabilities by offering enterprise-grade backporting services to maintain security in legacy production environments.

items.title: Introducing Mistral Large 4: Le chonk
items.one_liner: Mistral previews its 1-trillion parameter Mistral Large 4 model trained on NVIDIA Grace Blackwell GPUs.
items.summary: Mistral has released a preview of Mistral Large 4 via its API, a 1 trillion parameter model with 49 billion active parameters trained on a cluster of 3,800 NVIDIA Grace Blackwell GPUs. The open weights version is scheduled for release at the end of the month. The model introduces two reasoning levels—'none' and 'high'—and shows significant performance improvements over previous iterations, closing the gap with top frontier models.
items.bottom_line: Mistral Large 4 brings major performance gains and a 1-trillion parameter architecture to Mistral's API ahead of its open weights release.

The figures point to sustained growth rather than a one-off spike. Weekly attacks per organisation have climbed 36% in five months, from 2,055 in May. UK organisations faced an average of 1,920 attacks per week, a 50% increase year on year. Europe recorded the fastest growth of any region, with attacks up 61%, while Latin America faced the highest volume at 3,813 weekly attacks per organisation, followed by Africa (3,701) and APAC (3,593).

items.summary: Veteran Indian actor Nana Patekar has died suddenly at the age of 75 after suffering a cardiac arrest at his home in Goa. items.summary: Italy's parliament approved controversial electoral reforms championed by Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni's right-wing coalition by a vote of 227 to 164. The legislation shifts the country from a hybrid voting system to a fully proportional representation system while awarding 105 additional parliamentary seats to any coalition securing over 42% of the vote. The vote served as a confidence test for Meloni, whose coalition has maintained power since 2022 ahead of elections scheduled for next year.

items.summary: Mochamad Subchi Azal Tsani, an Indonesian former teacher convicted of sexual assault, has been returned to prison following an undercover investigation by the BBC that exposed his secret early release on parole. Tsani, the son of a prominent Islamic cleric, was originally sentenced to seven years in prison in 2022 for assaulting a student at an East Java boarding school. The BBC investigation revealed he was quietly paroled in August 2025 after serving less than half his sentence, without notifying the victim. The broadcast sparked intense public backlash, parliamentary scrutiny, and a government review that uncovered administrative irregularities. Consequently, his parole was revoked, and Immigration and Corrections Minister Agus Andrianto announced that officials responsible for the approval will face disciplinary sanctions.
items.bottom_line: A high-profile convicted sex offender in Indonesia was returned to prison after an investigative media report forced a government review and the revocation of his secret early parole.

items.one_liner: Widespread student protests across French high schools over underfunding and infrastructure issues have escalated into significant civil unrest.
items.summary: Student protests and high school blockages across France have turned violent, resulting in hundreds of injuries and numerous arrests amid anger over underfunding, teacher shortages, and dilapidated facilities in lycées. Although OECD data indicates that France spends more per upper-secondary student than the EU average and experiences milder teacher shortages than elsewhere, the discontent has manifested in unprecedented scale and unrest. items.title: Israelis demand accountability over 7 October failures three years after attacks
items.one_liner: Three years after the October 7 attacks, Israeli families are demanding an independent inquiry into intelligence failures and government accountability.
items.summary: Three years after the October 7, 2023 attacks by Hamas-led militants—the deadliest security failure in Israel's history—survivors and relatives of victims at Kibbutz Kfar Aza are intensifying demands for governmental accountability and an independent state inquiry. The attacks resulted in approximately 1,200 deaths and 251 hostages taken to Gaza, including half of Kfar Aza's civil defence squad and numerous intelligence personnel stationed near the border. Families argue that systemic intelligence failures and ignored pre-attack warnings from military observers and regional neighbors, such as the UAE, were overlooked by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's administration. items.title: CVE-2024-0244 – A heap buffer overflow in the Canon MF753Cdw printer
items.one_liner: A heap buffer overflow in Canon printer firmware demonstrates how obscure service drivers can be exploited for remote crashes or code execution.
items.summary: A researcher detailed the discovery of CVE-2024-0244, an unauthenticated heap-based buffer overflow in Canon MF753Cdw printers. The vulnerability exists in the fax driver's handling of SOAP messages sent to the /wsd/print endpoint. By sending a malformed payload with an oversized length field, an attacker can trigger an arbitrary free() operation, leading to a crash or potential code execution. The researcher leveraged UART access to debug the firmware and identify the vulnerable pointer.

items.title: Social Pain Disrupts Emotion-Action Brain-State Dynamics in Adolescents with Non-Suicidal Self-Injury
items.one_liner: An EEG and deep learning study on depressed adolescents identifies disrupted emotion-action brain-state dynamics during social pain as a neural signature for non-suicidal self-injury.
items.summary: Researchers combined an experimental pain paradigm, electroencephalography microstate analysis, and deep sequence modeling to investigate non-suicidal self-injury (NSSI) neurodynamics in 106 adolescents with depression. Social pain yielded the strongest NSSI discrimination with 68.55% accuracy, revealing weakened bidirectional transitions between specific microstates associated with emotional processing and action preparation. These findings identify disrupted emotion-action coupling as a key neurodynamic mechanism underlying altered social pain processing in NSSI. This approach provides a mechanistically interpretable neural signature for the objective identification of NSSI.
items.bottom_line: Disrupted emotion-action coupling during social pain serves as a measurable neural signature for identifying non-suicidal self-injury in adolescents.

items.summary: Spot gold recovered from a two-month low to trade near $4,120 an ounce as Chinese buyers returned from a weeklong holiday that had temporarily muted Asian market activity. Despite this rebound, bullion remained headed for a third consecutive weekly loss following a 1.3% drop prompted by reports that the White House was weighing military options against Iran. The precious metal has declined roughly 20% since the eruption of the US-Iran conflict in late February, as soaring energy costs stoke inflation and drive central banks to maintain tighter monetary policies. However, ongoing official sector purchases continue to provide structural price support, highlighted by the People's Bank of China adding 23 tons to its reserves in September. Meanwhile, traders continue monitoring Federal Reserve policy expectations, pricing in an 80% probability of a rate hike by December.
