items.title: Four compliance frameworks, one security team: Why fragmented university security raises regulatory risk
items.one_liner: Universities struggle with severe compliance pressure and tight reporting windows under overlapping federal privacy frameworks.
items.summary: Higher education institutions face severe regulatory complexity due to fragmented multi-campus environments combined with overlapping compliance frameworks like FERPA, GLBA, HIPAA, and CMMC. FERPA enforces a strict 24-hour window to report financial aid breaches to the Department of Education, creating immense pressure during incident response. Meanwhile, GLBA brings financial-sector safeguards and swift notification mandates for breaches affecting 500 or more consumers. Managing these overlapping rules across decentralized university IT systems amplifies operational risk.
items.bottom_line: Fragmented multi-campus university networks face high regulatory risk because frameworks like FERPA and GLBA mandate rapid breach notifications within 24 hours.

items.summary: Law firm Sheppard Mullin is facing a class-action lawsuit following the disclosure of a data breach. The firm has not yet provided specific details on the scale or nature of the compromised data. This legal action follows a growing trend of class-action litigation against organizations that suffer significant security incidents.
items.bottom_line: Sheppard Mullin is now the subject of a class-action lawsuit after disclosing a data breach.

items.title: Open source tool RemoveMacAI strips Apple Intelligence from macOS 27, reclaims up to 12 GB

items.title: Protesters blame 'vulture funds' for Spain's housing crisis
items.one_liner: Spain's severe housing crisis and soaring rental costs are fueling major protests, highlighting systemic market pressures relevant to real estate and broader economic trends.
items.summary: Protesters have been camping out in Madrid's Puerta del Sol square to protest Spain's housing crisis, blaming a lack of homes, landlords raising rents, and Airbnb. Demonstrators also point to investment funds and empty homes as major drivers of the crisis, a sentiment echoed by Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez who called a snap election after Congress rejected his emergency housing reforms. The movement was sparked by the case of 87-year-old Maricarmen Abascal, who was evicted after an investment firm raised her rent beyond her means, subsequently dying in hospital after the social backlash prompted an invitation to return. According to property outlet Idealista, rental costs in Spain have risen by an average of 84% over the last 10 years, with increases reaching 113% in central Málaga and nearly 150% in Marbella. A study by the Centre for Sociological Research showed widespread public support for higher taxes on owners of 10 or more properties, limits on short-term tourist accommodation, and the expropriation of empty homes.

Málaga rental increase: 113% in the city centre

items.title: Texas carries out first US execution since Christa Pike's botched lethal injections
items.one_liner: Texas executed Jamaal Howard via lethal injection despite legal challenges citing recent protocol failures in Tennessee.
items.summary: Texas has carried out the execution of 46-year-old Jamaal Howard using a lethal dose of pentobarbital at the state prison in Huntsville, marking the first US execution since a botched procedure involving Christa Pike in Tennessee the previous week. Howard's defense attorneys filed emergency appeals seeking a stay of execution, arguing that Texas intended to use the same drug from a potentially degraded supply that led to complications in Pike's case. State courts and the US Supreme Court denied the requests, and Governor Greg Abbott declined to grant a 30-day reprieve. With the rise of software-as-a-service (SaaS) companies in the late aughts, IT departments needed a way for users to authenticate to many new web services. SAML and the burgeoning single sign-on (SSO) industry fulfilled this need. However, SAML is being crushed under the weight of its own complexity. It’s time to deprecate it and move on to modern alternatives like OpenID Connect (OIDC).

items.title: Your AI agent doesn't know your codebase's context or constraints, and that's costing you
items.summary: An AI coding agent working in your repository has never seen your architecture. It has not read your intended module boundaries, your team's conventions, the incident that made you ban a certain pattern, or the reason one service is intended to call another and a third is not. It writes from the statistical average of everything it was trained on, which is a vast amount of other people's code and almost none of yours. So it produces code that compiles, passes a quick read, and quietly drifts away from how your system is actually built. That gap between "compiles" and "belongs" is not a matter of taste.
